items.title: Moonshot AI drops Kimi K3 open weights at 00:00 UTC July 27 (8pm ET July 26) — 2.8T-parameter MoE, 896 experts activating 16 per token (~50B live compute), 1M-token context, native video, Modified MIT license, ~594GB MXFP4 safetensors on Hugging Face; the largest open-weight model in AI history lands the same hour Washington is deciding whether to try to restrict it
items.summary: Moonshot AI released the full weights for Kimi K3 at 00:00 UTC on July 27, 2026 — roughly six hours before this snapshot went out — on Hugging Face under huggingface.co/moonshotai, under a Modified MIT license, exactly as promised on the July 16 API launch at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai. K3 is a 2.8-trillion-parameter Stable-LatentMoE with 896 experts, of which the router activates only 16 per token, giving roughly 50 billion parameters of live compute per forward pass. Context window is 1 million tokens, natively multimodal including video, and the native release is quantization-aware trained in MXFP4 four-bit precision — the ~594GB safetensors download IS the reference release, not a lossy re-quant. Community BF16 and GGUF re-quants are already being uploaded within hours. Practical hardware floor to load the full model in MXFP4 is 8× H100 80GB (or 4× H200 141GB, or 2× Blackwell B300, or an equivalent MI400 configuration) — a single RTX 4090 or Mac Studio cannot run full K3 even at four-bit. The API-launch benchmark set that has now been open-weights-verifiable since 00:00 UTC: SWE-bench Verified 76.8%, FrontierSWE 81.2, Terminal-Bench 2.1 88.3, Program Bench 77.8, SWE Marathon 42.0, BrowseComp 91.2, GPQA Diamond 93.5%, MMMU-Pro 81.6. On the LMArena Frontend Code leaderboard K3 debuted at #1 with a 1,679 score in blind preference testing, first in six of seven frontend sub-domains, ahead of Claude Fable 5. On Artificial Analysis's aggregate Intelligence Index K3 scores 57 and sits fourth of 189 models — behind Claude Fable 5 and two GPT-5.6 Sol reasoning settings, ahead of Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5 xhigh, Claude Sonnet 5, and GLM-5.2. Pricing on Moonshot's hosted API is $0.60/M input and $2.40/M output, roughly one-third of Claude Fable 5 and one-fifth of GPT-5.6 Sol at comparable output quality. The release lands into a policy situation that shaped up over the past 72 hours: the July 24 Jensen Huang-led open-weights letter now has 50 signatories (up from 25 on Friday, with OpenAI and Google flipping over the weekend, and Anthropic, Amazon, and xAI still not signed), and the Trump administration is reportedly considering an executive order, an Entity-List addition, security-threat advisories, or federal-procurement restrictions in response to K3 — but the fundamental technical fact of open weights is that once the ~594GB is on Hugging Face and torrent mirrors, it cannot be recalled.
items.why_it_matters: For Gabe: five reads. First, the specific 'largest open-weight model in AI history' read: 2.8 trillion total parameters, quantization-aware trained to MXFP4 native precision, released under a Modified MIT license on Hugging Face — this is the specific event where the frontier open-weights ceiling moved from ~1.6T (DeepSeek V4 Pro) to ~3T in a single drop, and the specific event where 'open weights are behind closed weights' stops being a defensible narrative on the aggregate Intelligence Index. K3 sitting fourth of 189 on Artificial Analysis puts it ahead of Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5 xhigh, and Claude Sonnet 5 — three closed-weights models most working developers were using as their default six weeks ago. Second, the specific 'you cannot run this locally' read: the practical hardware floor is 8× H100 80GB or equivalent. Even the MXFP4-native release at 594GB requires roughly 1.4TB of fast-tier memory to actually hold the weights, KV cache, and activations at working batch sizes. A single RTX 4090 (24GB) cannot run it. A Mac Studio M3 Ultra (192GB) cannot run it. What this specifically means for a hobbyist Python developer: the practical channels for running K3 are (a) hosted inference on OpenRouter, Together AI, Fireworks, Groq, or Cerebras (all of which will be routing K3 within days if not hours), (b) renting a Blackwell or H200 GPU cluster by the hour on Runpod, Vast.ai, or Lambda Labs, or (c) waiting for community distilled or pruned variants at the 70B-to-200B scale that CAN run on a single high-end workstation. The specific practical action item: if you want to try K3 tonight, the hosted-inference-via-OpenRouter path is the specific correct path, not the 'download the weights and run locally' path. Third, the specific policy-timing read that makes this a Monday-July-27 story: the release lands into an active Trump-administration deliberation about restricting Chinese open-weight AI (executive order, Entity List, procurement rules, sanctions under the Bessent Treasury framework announced July 21) — and the specific technical fact of the release is that restriction is now enforcement-impossible for anyone with a torrent client. Multiple analysts (Tom's Hardware, AI Governance Institute, FourWeekMBA) have consolidated around the specific framing that the July 27 midnight timing was chosen to establish 'the weights are already distributed' as a fait-accompli fact before Washington can respond with an executive order. The specific practical implication: even in the maximally restrictive-policy scenario, K3 will remain runnable on US developer infrastructure — the specific constraint would be that hosted-inference providers may not be able to offer it as a paid service. Fourth, the specific 'what to actually do with K3' read: on the SWE-bench Verified 76.8% and Terminal-Bench 2.1 88.3 benchmark reads, K3 is a specific 'coding-agent-quality open model' that is competitive with Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-5.5 for autonomous-agent workflows at roughly one-fifth the API cost. For a Python developer building anything with LangGraph, LlamaIndex, OpenRouter routing, or a homegrown ReAct loop, the specific action is: if your current default is Sonnet or GPT-5.5 for autonomous-tool-use paths, route one path to K3 this week and measure the cost-quality delta. The specific expectation is that for straightforward multi-step tool-use tasks (search + summarize + write code), K3 will be indistinguishable from your current default at ~20% of the cost. Fifth, the specific cascade-effect read for the rest of the week: within 24-48 hours, expect (a) hosted-inference providers (Together, Fireworks, Groq, Cerebras) to start offering K3 endpoints at $0.30-to-$0.50/M input pricing, (b) community BF16 and GGUF re-quants on Hugging Face optimized for consumer or workstation hardware, (c) a specific OpenRouter market-share spike as K3 becomes the new default low-cost frontier route (see the sibling OpenRouter item in this snapshot — the 46.4% Chinese-model share number is what will get updated to 55-60% by Friday), (d) an Anthropic public statement, either directly on the open-weights position or indirectly via a Claude-Opus-5 pricing or capability response, and (e) a specific Trump-administration policy announcement — most likely an Entity List addition of Moonshot rather than an outright ban, since the outright ban is now enforcement-impossible.

items.summary: The Nvidia-hosted 'Open Weights and American AI Leadership' letter, first published Thursday July 24 with 25 signatories and doubled to 50 by Sunday July 26 (with OpenAI and Google flipping over the weekend), stayed at 50 through Monday morning July 27, 2026 with Anthropic, Amazon, and xAI still absent — the same three organizations flagged as absentees on Sunday afternoon. The Monday-morning enrichment update: no new signatories, no removals, no Anthropic response of any kind. Digitimes, Startup Fortune, Lanka Biznews, Corenexis, and Digital Applied have consolidated around a specific Monday-morning framing that treats the Kimi K3 weight release six hours ago as the specific stress-test event for Anthropic's closed-weights position — the letter argues open weights strengthen safety, cybersecurity, and sovereignty; the K3 release ~594GB safetensors under Modified MIT license actually delivers that at frontier scale; Anthropic's position that open source is 'a red herring' (Dario Amodei) now has to survive a working counter-example that ranks fourth of 189 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index. Digitimes specifically frames the letter as 'Nvidia backs open-weight AI as OpenAI, Anthropic lobby for tighter controls' — the specific claim being that Anthropic and (previously) OpenAI have been actively lobbying the Trump administration for the Kimi K3 restriction package, which is a more aggressive positioning than 'chose not to sign a pro-open-weights letter.' The specific Monday-morning structural read: Anthropic is now the only US frontier lab whose stated policy position (weights once released cannot be recalled or made safe) is publicly at odds with the working evidence on Hugging Face (K3 weights are on Hugging Face, and both the US developer stack via OpenRouter and the US government via any imaginable executive order will now have to live with that fact). The weekend-of-July-25-26 snapshot captured in yesterday's pm digest showed Chinese models at 46.4% of platform-wide tokens vs 35.7% for US models. Updated Monday-morning figures (Dataconomy Feb 2026 baseline of 61%, eWeek 60% US-business-only slice, Yahoo Finance 63% during first week of July for US-enterprise slice) show that the 46.4% platform-wide number is now specifically the LOWER-BOUND estimate — the US-enterprise-and-US-business slices where OpenRouter usage is heaviest sit in the 58-to-63% range. Chinese models still hold eight of the top ten most-used models on OpenRouter with only Anthropic's Claude family (aggregate 13.3% token share) remaining as a US-lab representative in the top ten. OpenAI and Google both remain out of the top ten entirely. The specific Kimi-K3 update overnight: with K3 weights now live on Hugging Face and hosted-inference providers (Together, Fireworks, Groq, Cerebras) expected to route K3 within 24-48 hours at $0.30-to-$0.50/M input pricing, the OpenRouter Chinese-model share is expected to climb further this week as K3 debuts as the new default frontier-tier low-cost route. The specific price-mechanism read is unchanged and reinforced: DeepSeek V4 Flash at $0.14/M input, Kimi K2.7 at $0.35/M input, Kimi K3 hosted-API at $0.60/M input (with re-routed Together/Fireworks pricing likely to land at $0.30-0.50/M) vs OpenAI GPT-5.5 at $5.00/M and Claude Opus 5 at $12/M is a specific 8x-to-90x price differential that maps directly to the token-volume shift.
